title: Embedded systems
starter: List five devices in your home that contain a computer but don't look like one. What does each one do with the data it collects?
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: What is an embedded system?
facts: A computer system built into a larger device.
It has a dedicated function: it does one job, or a small set of jobs.
Examples: washing machines, microwaves, traffic lights and car engine management.
stations.challenge: Explain what an embedded system is.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A computer system built into a larger device.
Also credit: It has a dedicated function: it does one job, or a small set of jobs.

questions.a: A computer system built into a larger device to do a dedicated job

questions.q: Which is an example of an embedded system?
questions.a: The controller in a microwave oven

stations.name: Characteristics
facts: Limited functions: runs one dedicated program.
Usually small, low power and cheap to mass produce.
Very reliable, and often has to respond in real time.
stations.challenge: Why are embedded systems usually cheap and low power?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Limited functions: runs one dedicated program.
Also credit: Usually small, low power and cheap to mass produce.

questions.q: Which are typical characteristics of embedded systems? Select all that apply.
questions.a: Dedicated to a specific task; Low power consumption; Small in size; Reliable

questions.q: Why are embedded systems usually cheap to make?
questions.a: They only need enough processing power for one job, and are made in huge numbers

stations.name: Embedded systems everywhere
facts: At home: washing machines, microwaves, smart thermostats, TVs and fridges.
Out and about: traffic lights, cash machines and car systems, like automatic lights and anti-lock brakes.
On you: fitness trackers and smartwatches.
stations.challenge: List five embedded systems you have used today.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: At home: washing machines, microwaves, smart thermostats, TVs and fridges.
Also credit: Out and about: traffic lights, cash machines and car systems, like automatic lights and anti-lock brakes.

questions.q: Which of these contains an embedded system?

stations.name: Input, process, output
facts: Input: buttons, dials and sensors, such as a water temperature sensor.
Process: a microcontroller runs the program and makes decisions.
Output: motors, heaters, lights and displays.
stations.challenge: Choose a device in your home and describe its inputs, its processing and its outputs.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Input: buttons, dials and sensors, such as a water temperature sensor.
Also credit: Process: a microcontroller runs the program and makes decisions.

questions.q: Is each part of a washing machine an input, process or output?
questions.a: Program dial = Input; Temperature sensor = Input; Microcontroller running the wash program = Process; Motor turning the drum = Output; Water heater = Output; Display showing time left = Output

stations.name: Programming embedded systems
facts: The program is stored permanently in the device, often called firmware.
Embedded systems are often programmed in C or C++, which run fast and give close control of the hardware.
Some firmware can be updated, like a smart TV's software update.
stations.challenge: What programming language is mainly used for embedded systems, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: The program is stored permanently in the device, often called firmware.
Also credit: Embedded systems are often programmed in C or C++, which run fast and give close control of the hardware.

questions.q: Which programming language is mainly used for embedded systems?

questions.a: The program stored permanently in a device to control it

stations.name: Embedded or general purpose?
facts: A general-purpose computer, like a laptop, can run many different programs.
An embedded system is built in to one device and does one dedicated job.
Some devices blur the line, like smart TVs that run apps.
stations.challenge: Explain why a laptop is not an embedded system.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A general-purpose computer, like a laptop, can run many different programs.
Also credit: An embedded system is built in to one device and does one dedicated job.

questions.q: Why is a laptop not an embedded system?
questions.a: It's a general-purpose computer that can run many different programs

questions.q: A car has a computer that only controls the anti-lock brakes. What is it?

final.name: Final challenge: spot the embedded system

questions.q: Is each device an embedded system or a general-purpose computer?
questions.a: Washing machine = Embedded; Microwave oven = Embedded; Traffic lights = Embedded; Car anti-lock brakes = Embedded; Smart thermostat = Embedded; Laptop = General purpose; Desktop PC = General purpose; Tablet running apps = General purpose

Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
